winners.premise: A groom admits sleeping with the bride's bridesmaid during their engagement and tries to make the wedding depend on the bridesmaid's pregnancy test.
winners.conflict: A bride must decide whether the absence of a pregnancy can excuse the betrayal her groom has already admitted.
winners.twist: The bridesmaid reports a negative test, but the result does not erase either adult's choice to have an affair during the engagement.
winners.hook: My groom admitted he'd slept with my bridesmaid during our engagement. Then he tried to make our wedding depend on her pregnancy test.
winners.narration: Tom asked me to make Rina take one before the ceremony. I asked why I should arrange that. He said they'd slept together twice since our engagement, but there might be nothing to worry about. I put down my earrings and asked what he meant by nothing. He said that if she wasn't pregnant, we could deal with it privately after the honeymoon. I called Rina myself. She said she'd already taken a test and it was negative. I didn't ask her to prove it. I asked whether what Tom had told me about the affair was true. She said yes, then started apologizing. Tom heard the word negative and said we could stop panicking. I told him the test hadn't answered the question I'd asked her. He said everyone was arriving, the food was paid for, and we couldn't throw the whole wedding away over something that hadn't resulted in a child. I asked whether he was sorry he'd slept with her or relieved he thought there wouldn't be a consequence. He said that wasn't fair. I said a test result wasn't the condition for my vows. I called my mother and asked her to come upstairs. We weren't going ahead with the ceremony. I left the earrings beside the mirror. Whatever that test said, I already knew what he'd done.
winners.title: The Answer He Wanted Before Their Wedding
winners.description: The groom wants a pregnancy result before the ceremony. The bride needs an answer about the affair he has already admitted.
winners.payoff: Whatever that test said, I already knew what he'd done.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF A RESULT CANNOT ERASE BETRAYAL

winners.premise: A sister hires a fake debt collector to demand money from her sibling at work even though she is the one who owes the sibling six thousand dollars.
winners.conflict: A woman must protect her reputation at work while her sister uses public embarrassment to escape repaying a family loan.
winners.twist: The supposed collector is a paid performer, and the sister hopes reversing the debt in front of coworkers will make the real lender stop asking.
winners.hook: My sister hired a fake debt collector to demand money from me at work. She was the one who owed me six thousand dollars.
winners.narration: He stood at our shop counter and said I was refusing to repay Beth. My manager asked him to lower his voice. I asked what company he represented. He said Beth had sent him and that we should discuss payment where my coworkers could hear. I said she'd borrowed six thousand from me for rent. He looked at his phone, then asked whether I was saying she'd given him the wrong story. I called her and put her on speaker. She told me not to make a scene. I asked why she'd sent him to my job. She said she'd paid him to act like a collector because I wouldn't stop asking her for repayment. She thought I'd understand how humiliating it felt to be chased. I asked whether she'd needed to invent a debt to make her point. She said I could still afford to wait. My manager told the man the performance was over and asked him to leave. Beth said I was turning everyone against her. I said she'd chosen the audience. She hadn't repaid anything, and we still needed a real conversation about when she could. But my coworkers now knew which way the money had gone. I went back to serving customers. Next time she called, I listened before discussing another deadline. I wasn't agreeing the loan had disappeared.
winners.title: Six Thousand Dollars at the Shop Counter
winners.description: A stranger arrives at her workplace to demand repayment. The sister who sent him has reversed the story about who borrowed the money.
winners.payoff: I wasn't agreeing the loan had disappeared.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF EMBARRASSMENT DOES NOT CANCEL A DEBT

winners.premise: An employee finds overtime he never worked on his payslip, and his manager asks him to withdraw the extra money and hand it over in cash.
winners.conflict: An employee who needs the money must refuse to let his wage record conceal his manager's personal withdrawal from the company.
winners.twist: The manager offers a small share for cooperating, turning an apparent payroll windfall into a request to endorse work that never happened.
winners.hook: I found overtime I'd never worked on my payslip. My boss wanted me to withdraw the extra money and give it to him.
winners.narration: There were four hundred extra dollars under hours I hadn't done. I asked Gary whether payroll had made a mistake. He said he'd added hours because the team had budget left. Then he told me to bring the extra cash in the next morning. The company paid our wages. I asked why his money needed hours in my name. He said it was just paperwork and I shouldn't make a favor complicated. I needed money for a repair at home, and for a moment I'd thought the payment might mean someone had finally noticed my work. Now he said I could keep fifty dollars for helping. I asked whether he expected me to confirm I'd worked those hours. He said nobody would ask unless I gave them a reason. I told him I wasn't confirming work I hadn't done. He said I could forget any real overtime if I wanted to be difficult about this. I left the extra money untouched and contacted payroll with the hours I'd actually worked. They said they would correct the payment and asked who had submitted the extra hours. I gave them Gary's name. I didn't know what he'd say when they called him. That afternoon, he wouldn't speak to me. I clocked out at six. That was the time I was willing to put my name beside.
winners.title: The Overtime He Wanted Back in Cash
winners.description: Extra pay initially looks like welcome recognition. Then the manager explains who should keep the money and whose name should stay on the hours.
winners.payoff: That was the time I was willing to put my name beside.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HIS NAME SHOULD MATCH HIS WORK

winners.premise: A tour guide asks visitors to sponsor his own son as an orphan, then scolds the boy for calling him Dad.
winners.conflict: A visitor must confront a false fundraising story without treating the child's genuine needs or his relationship with his parents as part of the deception.
winners.twist: Both parents are alive and the worn-out shoes are real, so honest help does not require the child to pretend he has nobody.
winners.hook: Our tour guide asked us to sponsor his son as an orphan. Then he told the boy off for calling him Dad.
winners.narration: Sam brought us to a village school. He pointed to a boy whose shoes were splitting at the toes and said he'd lost both parents. Then the boy tugged his sleeve and called him Dad. Sam told him to remember what they'd discussed. I asked why he'd said that. He admitted the boy was his son and both parents were alive. His wife arrived with their son's lunch. I asked whether she was his mother. Sam said yes, and that people gave more readily if they thought a child had nobody. Another visitor said we should leave without giving anything. Sam asked whether his son's feet mattered less because he'd lied. I said the shoes mattered. Making his son pretend his parents were dead mattered too. The boy asked whether he was in trouble for forgetting. Sam started saying he'd explained the story at home, then stopped when his wife asked what story. He told the boy he hadn't done anything wrong. I asked whether they wanted help buying school shoes, without the orphan story. His mother said yes. We went with them to a nearby shop. Sam knelt to check the fit and tied the new laces. His son stood beside him in shoes that fit. He didn't have to pretend he was alone to deserve them.
winners.title: The Shoes in the Orphan Story
winners.description: A visitor catches the guide lying about a child's parents. The lie is false, but the child's need for school shoes is real.
winners.payoff: He didn't have to pretend he was alone to deserve them.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HONEST HELP STILL MATTERS
